text: After this you can identify each billing component and explain how it is calculated.

Examine a bill as separate quantities: consumption, measured maximum demand, fixed fees, and time-dependent prices. Electricity demand is commonly calculated from an average over a specified meter interval, not one instantaneous peak. Power factor compares real power with apparent power; load factor compares average demand with peak demand. The time when electricity is used may affect the bill even when total kWh stays unchanged.

items: Record each billed quantity and its unit. You should see: A monthly list of energy and peak demand. If not: Check that demand is not labelled kWh.
Copy each rate and fixed fee. You should see: Energy, demand, and other charge categories. If not: Ask the utility for the tariff rules.
Check multiplication and billed periods. You should see: A subtotal that matches the tariff logic. If not: Record differences without assuming billing error.
